::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## What this page does

Use this page to change ordinary public website content: explanatory text, links, images, page metadata or navigation.

> **Stata creates approved analytical products. Quarto presents them.** Do not recalculate or correct surveillance results in a QMD file.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Procedure at a glance"}
1. Start an editing session and create a development branch.
2. Edit the public source file and check the local preview.
3. Run a complete local render and inspect the affected pages.
4. Commit and merge the branch using [Render and publish the website](render-publish.qmd).
:::

## Before you start

Confirm that any required data package or report has already completed its controlled Stata approval and publication route. The website may use only approved public products in `site/`.

Start `start-info-hub-edit.bat`, update local `main`, and create a development branch as described in [Render and publish the website](render-publish.qmd). Identify the public source file that owns the content before making a change.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Input files and public source

| File or source | What to check |
|---|---|
| `site/**/*.qmd` | The public page source. Open the page that owns the text, link or layout you need to change. |
| `site/downloads/files/**` | Optional approved public download or figure. Link only to the approved website copy, never to a private location. |
| `site/assets/**` | Optional public image, stylesheet or other ordinary website asset. Confirm it is suitable for public release. |
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Code and configuration files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| The selected `site/**/*.qmd` file | Quarto source file edited directly for ordinary page changes. |
| `site/_quarto.yml` | Site-wide configuration, navigation and sidebars. Edit only for a genuine site-wide change. |
| `site/scripts/build_download_catalogue.py` | Runs automatically before each complete render. Do not run or edit it for an ordinary content change. |
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Output files

| File or folder | Result |
|---|---|
| `site/_site/` | Generated local website created by `quarto render`. Inspect it, but do not edit or commit it. |
| `site/downloads/downloads.yml` | Generated central Downloads catalogue. The normal render updates it only when an approved catalogue record changes; never edit it by hand. |
:::

## Step 1: Open the source page

In VS Code Explorer, open the relevant file beneath `site/`.

Read the title and YAML header before editing. If the page links to a generated analytical figure, table or download, confirm that the target is the approved public website copy.

Do not edit anything in `site/_site/`: it is generated by Quarto.

## Step 2: Make the smallest required change

Edit the QMD directly for ordinary public content, such as explanatory text, headings, public methods notes, links, page metadata, captions or ordinary layout.

For a navigation change, edit `site/_quarto.yml` only when the change genuinely affects site-wide navigation. A YAML error can affect the whole site.

Do not enter analytical values in a QMD when an approved generated product owns them. If a number, figure, disclosure decision or download is wrong, return to the relevant analytical workflow and publish a corrected approved package.

## Step 3: Save and check the local preview

Save the file. The preview started by `start-info-hub-edit.bat` should refresh in Firefox.

Check the changed page for wording, headings, tables, figures, links and normal-window readability. If you changed metadata or `_quarto.yml`, also check the affected listing, navbar or sidebar.

## Step 4: Run a complete local render

Open a new **VS Code PowerShell terminal** with **Terminal > New Terminal**. From the repository root, enter:

```powershell
.\venv-info-hub\Scripts\Activate.ps1
cd site
quarto render
```

The render runs the Downloads catalogue builder and then refreshes `site/_site/`. A successful render completes without an error message. It does **not** deploy the website.

## Step 5: Check automatically refreshed website products

Some products refresh from approved public files during the normal render. **No separate refresh action is required.**

After the render, check any affected product:

| Product | What to do |
|---|---|
| CVD dashboards and tables | Confirm that the page displays the approved public data. See [dashboard refresh](../workflows/reporting/dashboard-regeneration.qmd) or [table refresh](../workflows/reporting/tabulation-regeneration.qmd) for technical reference. |
| Downloads page | Confirm that the expected public data package appears once and that its ZIP opens. See [how the Downloads page refreshes](../workflows/reporting/downloads-page-regeneration.qmd). |
| Quarto listings | Open the listing and check the title, date, description and ordering created from page metadata. |

Do not hand-edit `site/downloads/downloads.yml`, generated listings or any file beneath `site/_site/`.

## Step 6: Publish the approved website change

When the local render and review are satisfactory, follow [Render and publish the website](render-publish.qmd) to inspect the Git changes, commit the development branch, merge the pull request and check the live site.
